title: Dead Man's Folly

vibeProfile.oneLine: A pretend murder hunt at a village fete becomes a real one.

summary: Invited to help stage a pretend murder hunt at a grand country-house fete, the mystery writer Ariadne Oliver senses something genuinely wrong, and calls in Hercule Poirot. She is right: the girl playing the victim is found really dead. Set among the gardens and boathouses of a Devon estate, it is a warm, clever late Christie that gently sends up the whole business of detective fiction even as it delivers a satisfying one.
whyReadIt: A country-house fete, a staged murder that turns real, and Christie teasing her own genre. Cosy and clever.

funFacts.text: Ariadne Oliver, the mystery novelist in the book, is widely read as Christie's affectionate self-portrait.
